title: Why you can't remember being a baby
voiceover: You can't remember being a baby... and it's not because nothing happened. It's because your brain was deleting everything. The part of your brain that stores long-term memories, the hippocampus, isn't fully developed until around age three or four. Before that, you're forming memories... but your brain literally has no way to file them. Even weirder: scientists think rapid neuron growth in babies actively erases old memories to make room for new connections. So somewhere in there, you had a favorite toy, a first word, a real personality... and your own brain wiped it. Follow for one mind-blowing fact a day.
